paras: The killing of Jim Nichols was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Constable Hugo Schultz at a cabin in Oldham County, Kentucky, on or about September 6, 1903, during an attempt to arrest his brother Will. Nichols died twelve days later; the Louisville Courier-Journal reported that a posse had threatened "mob violence" against his brother.

The arrest followed the shooting of William Smith, a Louisville and Eastern electric-car conductor, on September 5 at Houston's station. Smith said that Will Nichols, whom he had put off the car, fired three shots at its return, one hitting him in the thigh.

Schultz traced Will Nichols the next morning to a cabin near Brownsboro holding five Black men. By the constable's side of events, Jim Nichols "jumped at" Schultz and seized his revolver; Schultz wrenched it free and shot him in the left breast. Will Nichols then fired a shotgun from the doorway, missed, and barred the door.

Marshal Marion Spears of Pewee Valley and Constable Ad Hall arrived with a posse of about twenty-five, which officers had to restrain from "mob violence." Will Nichols surrendered on a promise of protection and was jailed on a charge of malicious shooting with intent to kill.
At the jail he denied shooting Smith and said he had not been on the car. Jim Nichols died on or about September 18, and no report of an inquest, an inquiry into the shooting, or a trial was found.

Only the Courier-Journal was found to cover the episode, on September 7 and 19. Its first story, headed "MOB VIOLENCE ATTEMPTED" and "CONSTABLE SCHULTZ'S FEAT," told events from the constable's and conductor's side and described "Five large negroes" in the cabin. The death notice, "WOUND IS FATAL. Negro Dies After Two Weeks of Suffering," said Nichols was shot "while trying to prevent the arrest of his brother." No Black newspaper account was found.
The first report places the cabin near Brownsboro, while the death notice puts Will Nichols's home "near Forest." The notice also says only that Nichols was shot during the struggle.

reader.title: Killing of Jim Nichols
bases: A constable shot Jim Nichols while trying to arrest his brother on a shooting charge; the gathering posse's threatened 'mob violence' was restrained and harmed no one (A1, A2).
Both reports come from one paper, the Louisville Courier-Journal, and the first rests on the constable's and conductor's accounts (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Constable's account (as told by the Courier-Journal)
accounts.gist: Jim Nichols jumped at Schultz as he entered, grabbed his revolver, and the pistol discharged in the struggle; Schultz wrenched it away and fired, hitting Nichols in the left breast.

accounts.label: Conductor's account
accounts.gist: Smith said four Black men flagged the car at Houston's, he was knocked down, and Will Nichols fired three shots, the third striking him.

accounts.label: Will Nichols's statement
accounts.gist: At the jail he denied shooting Smith and said he was not on the car at the time; the report breaks off there.

accounts.label: Death notice
accounts.gist: Jim Nichols was shot while trying to prevent his brother's arrest, during a struggle for the constable's revolver.

framing.detail: The Courier-Journal headed its first story 'CONSTABLE SCHULTZ'S FEAT' and said Schultz shot 'only after he had been fired upon', telling the event from the officer's and conductor's side.
The death notice, 'WOUND IS FATAL. Negro Dies After Two Weeks of Suffering', restated the struggle without comment.
